title: [review] project-LICHEN-worker6-p6n9: C EDHOC TH_2 byte ordering differs from Rust / RFC 9529 vectors
description:
## Bug

`lichen/subsys/lichen/edhoc/edhoc.c` computes TH_2 as `SHA-256(H(msg1) || G_Y || C_R)` with raw memcpy:

Initiator (lines 720-728): `memcpy(th2_input, h_msg1, 32) || memcpy(th2_input+32, g_y, 32) || memcpy(th2_input+64, c_r, c_r_len)`

Responder (lines 1166-1174): same pattern with `eph_pk` instead of `g_y`.

The Rust implementation (`rust/lichen-oscore/src/edhoc.rs:407-414`) does `SHA-256(G_Y || H(message_1))` — different ordering and excludes C_R (C_R coverage is implicit in the RFC 9529 signature trace). The Rust implementation matches known RFC 9529 test vectors.

The C `compute_th()` helper (line 72) already does proper CBOR encoding for TH_3/TH_4 but the TH_2 code path bypasses it entirely.
